introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Brama and your address CES de Nyapang.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the picture.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan:** letter to a friend (informal register, *tu*): address and date, salutation; reasons for his giving up; advice; reasons why he should continue; closing formula and signature.

**Tense chosen:** the présent for the situation, the passé composé for what the friend said, the futur simple for the consequences and the impératif for the advice (an informal letter, so *tu* is used).

**Model essay** (148 words)

CES de Nyapang, le 15 juin

Cher Abdou,

J'ai appris avec tristesse que tu arrêtais tes études. Tu m'as dit que tes parents n'avaient plus d'argent, que les cours te semblaient trop difficiles et que tu voulais travailler. Je comprends ta situation, mais je te demande de revenir sur ta décision.

Voici mes conseils : parle à ton père et à tes professeurs, car certains élèves reçoivent une bourse. Travaille aussi chaque soir avec moi ; je t'aiderai en mathématiques.

Tu dois continuer, car un diplôme t'ouvrira les portes d'un bon métier. Sans études, tu auras peu de choix et tu regretteras ta décision plus tard. Tu es intelligent et tu peux réussir. Pense à ton avenir et à la fierté de tes parents.

Je suis certain que tu trouveras une solution avec l'aide de l'école. Reviens en classe lundi, s'il te plaît. Ton ami t'attend.

Amicalement,
Brama

**Notes**

The letter gives the writer's name (Brama) and address (CES de Nyapang) as the topic requires. It covers the three points: the reasons for the friend's decision (no money, difficult lessons, wish to work), advice (talk to his father and teachers, ask for a scholarship, work together every evening) and the reasons why he should continue (a diploma opens the way to a good job, he is intelligent, regret later). The recipient's name and the date are invented; the topic does not impose them.

Word count: the whole letter, including the address line, the date, the salutation and the signature, has 148 words; without the names, the abbreviation and the date it has 142 words, so the 140 to 150 limits are respected either way.

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing a continuous text with no address, date, salutation or closing formula, or signing with another name than the one imposed (Brama).
2. Mixing *tu* and *vous* in the same letter.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *ensuite*, *enfin*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All the bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |
